parameters.query: UPDATE upload_batches SET status = 'matching' WHERE batch_id = $1::uuid RETURNING batch_id;

-- STAGE 1: set-based SQL pre-filter. One statement evaluates every (new user x active product) pair inside Postgres.
-- Hard filters (age, employment, max score) are applied first; income/score allow a small tolerance band so that
-- "near misses" can be judged later. Exact matches are approved immediately, near misses are queued for the LLM.
WITH pairs AS (
  SELECT u.user_id, p.product_id,
         (u.monthly_income >= p.min_monthly_income AND u.credit_score >= p.min_credit_score) AS exact_ok
  FROM users u
  JOIN loan_products p
    ON p.is_active
   AND u.age BETWEEN COALESCE(p.min_age, 18) AND COALESCE(p.max_age, 100)
   AND (p.allowed_employment IS NULL OR u.employment_status = ANY(p.allowed_employment))
   AND (p.max_credit_score IS NULL OR u.credit_score <= p.max_credit_score)
  WHERE u.upload_batch_id = $1::uuid
    AND u.monthly_income >= p.min_monthly_income * 0.90
    AND u.credit_score  >= p.min_credit_score - 20
), ins AS (
  INSERT INTO matches (user_id, product_id, batch_id, status, stage)
  SELECT user_id, product_id, $1::uuid,
         CASE WHEN exact_ok THEN 'approved' ELSE 'review' END,
         CASE WHEN exact_ok THEN 'sql_exact' ELSE 'sql_near_miss' END
  FROM pairs
  ON CONFLICT (user_id, product_id) DO UPDATE SET
    batch_id = EXCLUDED.batch_id, status = EXCLUDED.status, stage = EXCLUDED.stage,
    llm_reason = NULL, rank = NULL, notified = false, created_at = now()
  RETURNING status
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE upload_batch_id = $1::uuid) AS users_in_batch,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM loan_products WHERE is_active) AS active_products,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE upload_batch_id = $1::uuid) * (SELECT count(*) FROM loan_products WHERE is_active) AS naive_pairs,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'approved') AS approved_by_sql,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'review')   AS near_miss_for_llm
FROM ins;

-- STAGE 2: only near-miss pairs (typically a tiny fraction of all pairs) are fetched for LLM judgement.
SELECT m.match_id, u.monthly_income, u.credit_score, u.employment_status, u.age,
       p.product_name, p.provider, p.interest_rate, p.min_monthly_income, p.min_credit_score, p.eligibility_text
FROM matches m
JOIN users u ON u.user_id = m.user_id
JOIN loan_products p ON p.product_id = m.product_id
WHERE m.batch_id = $1::uuid AND m.status = 'review'
ORDER BY m.match_id
LIMIT 200;

parameters.query:
UPDATE matches m
SET status = CASE WHEN v.eligible THEN 'approved' ELSE 'rejected' END,
    stage = 'llm_judged', llm_reason = v.reason
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS v(match_id bigint, eligible boolean, reason text)
WHERE m.match_id = v.match_id
RETURNING m.match_id;

-- STAGE 4: rank approved matches per user (exact matches first, then lowest interest rate).
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT m.match_id,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY m.user_id
                            ORDER BY (m.stage = 'sql_exact') DESC, p.interest_rate ASC) AS rn
  FROM matches m JOIN loan_products p ON p.product_id = m.product_id
  WHERE m.batch_id = $1::uuid AND m.status = 'approved'
), upd AS (
  UPDATE matches m SET rank = r.rn FROM ranked r WHERE m.match_id = r.match_id RETURNING m.match_id
)
SELECT count(*) AS ranked_matches FROM upd;
UPDATE upload_batches SET status = 'matched', matched_at = now() WHERE batch_id = $1::uuid RETURNING batch_id;

parameters.content:
**Workflow B - Multi-stage matching (Optimization Treasure Hunt)**

Naive: users x products pairs -> one LLM call each (slow, costly).

Stage 1 SQL pre-filter: hard rules for ALL pairs in one set-based query. Exact matches approved instantly.
Stage 2: only near-misses (<=10% income / <=20 score short) are fetched.
Stage 3: near-misses are BATCHED (25 per LLM call). LLM down -> conservative reject.
Stage 4: rank per user, mark batch matched, trigger workflow C.
